rationale: The candidate reads as one coherent primary mass with decent silhouette control, and it does respond to the parcel better than a box-filling extrusion. However, the visible form is still essentially a compact tilted block with very little legible public void, court, or entry seam at the verified road frontage. For neighborhood living / mixed neighborhood program, the semantic contract asks for an active ground threshold and at least one clear public void or terrace; this candidate instead seals the frontage and keeps the access response weak and semantically opposite. The section is also not doing enough work: no convincing carved ground, lifted edge, or terrace logic is visible across views. So the mass is coherent, but not program-fit. The references support a compact commercial street building with an open court or softened threshold, which the candidate currently lacks. The counterfactual bridge reference suggests a transferable operation: introduce a cut/notch or courtyard aligned to the access edge, preserving the dominant mass while creating an explicit public seam.
